# Swoosh research — answers per question

All citations point to current `main` (v1.27.1) unless otherwise noted. The `hexdocs.pm/swoosh` per-module pages are slightly behind (`Loops` shows v1.25.1, `Mailpit` is on 1.27.0+); GitHub `main` is the canonical source. Latest release is **1.27.1** (lib/swoosh.ex `@version`); previously released versions in our range: 1.26.x, 1.25.x, 1.19.x, 1.18.x.

URL legend used below:
- M = https://hexdocs.pm/swoosh/Swoosh.html
- Loops = https://hexdocs.pm/swoosh/Swoosh.Adapters.Loops.html (source: github.com/swoosh/swoosh/blob/main/lib/swoosh/adapters/loops.ex)
- Mailpit = https://hexdocs.pm/swoosh/Swoosh.Adapters.Mailpit.html (source: github.com/swoosh/swoosh/blob/main/lib/swoosh/adapters/mailpit.ex)
- Finch = https://hexdocs.pm/swoosh/Swoosh.ApiClient.Finch.html (source: github.com/swoosh/swoosh/blob/main/lib/swoosh/api_client/finch.ex)
- ApiClient = https://hexdocs.pm/swoosh/Swoosh.ApiClient.html
- Mailer = https://hexdocs.pm/swoosh/Swoosh.Mailer.html
- TA = https://hexdocs.pm/swoosh/Swoosh.TestAssertions.html
- Test = https://hexdocs.pm/swoosh/Swoosh.Adapters.Test.html
- DeliveryError = https://hexdocs.pm/swoosh/Swoosh.DeliveryError.html
- mix.exs = https://github.com/swoosh/swoosh/blob/main/mix.exs
- changelog = https://github.com/swoosh/swoosh/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

---

## 1. Swoosh.Adapters.Loops

- **Module name:** `Swoosh.Adapters.Loops` (added in **1.18.0** — changelog: "Implement loops.so adapter @caioaao (#1012)").
- **Required config:** `[:api_key]` (via `use Swoosh.Adapter, required_config: [:api_key]`).
- **Optional:** `base_url` — default `"https://app.loops.so/api/v1"`, endpoint appended `"/transactional"`.
- **HTTP:** `POST {base_url}/transactional`, headers = `[{"Content-Type","application/json"}, {"User-Agent","swoosh/<ver>"}, {"Authorization","Bearer <api_key>"}]`.
- **Payload mapping (verbatim from `lib/swoosh/adapters/loops.ex`):**

```elixir
defp prepare_payload(email) do
  %{}
  |> prepare_to(email)
  |> prepare_provider_options_payload_fields(email)
  |> prepare_attachments(email)
end

defp prepare_to(payload, %Email{to: to}),
  do: Map.put(payload, "email", render_recipient(to))

defp prepare_provider_options_payload_fields(payload, %Email{provider_options: provider_options}) do
  Map.merge(payload, %{
    "transactionalId" => provider_options.transactional_id,
    "addToAudience"   => provider_options[:add_to_audience?] || false,
    "dataVariables"   => provider_options[:data_variables] || %{}
  })
end
```

- **Where fields come from:** both `transactionalId` and `dataVariables` come **exclusively from `provider_options`**, not from `subject` / `headers` / anywhere else on `%Swoosh.Email{}`. You set them with `put_provider_option/3`:

```elixir
import Swoosh.Email
new()
|> to("katy@example.com")
|> from("IGNORED")                       # required by Swoosh, IGNORED by Loops API
|> put_provider_option(:transactional_id, "clfq6dinn000yl70fgwwyp82l")
|> put_provider_option(:data_variables, %{"name" => "Chris", "passwordResetLink" => "..."})
|> put_provider_option(:add_to_audience?, true)
```

- `email.subject`, `email.html_body`, `email.text_body`, `email.headers`, `email.cc`, `email.bcc`, `email.reply_to`, `email.attachments` are **all ignored** by the Loops adapter — the email body is rendered server-side from the `transactionalId` template plus `dataVariables`. Attachments ARE supported but only if Loops has enabled them on the account; mapping is `%{"filename"=>filename, "contentType"=>content_type, "data"=>Base64.encode(...)}`.
- **Return shape (api_client):** `200..399` → `{:ok, %{}}`; `>=400` → `{:error, {code, decoded_or_raw_body}}`; network → `{:error, reason}`.
- **Important gap:** the Loops HTTP API natively accepts an `Idempotency-Key` request header (returns 409 on replay inside 24h) — but the Swoosh adapter does **not** emit it. `email.header("Idempotency-Key", ...)` will not be passed through (see Q7). The only built-in workaround is `put_provider_option(:idempotency_key, ...)` and a small fork/patch — current upstream has no such provider_option.
- Source: `lib/swoosh/adapters/loops.ex` on `main`.

---

## 2. Swoosh.Adapters.Mailpit

- **Module name:** `Swoosh.Adapters.Mailpit`. **Introduced in v1.26.0** (GitHub releases page: "Added adapter for self-hosted Mailpit @waseigo (#1152)").
- **Required config:** `[:base_url]`. **Optional:** `api_key` (when set, sent as `Authorization: Basic <api_key>`).
- **No default port baked in** — you must set `base_url:` explicitly (e.g. `"http://localhost:8025"` for the standard Mailpit dev port, or your own).
- **HTTP:** `POST {base_url}/api/v1/send`, `Content-Type: application/json`, `Accept: application/json`, `User-Agent: swoosh/<ver>`, optional `Authorization: Basic <api_key>`.
- **Body fields sent (from `prepare_body/1`):** `From`, `To` (list of `{Name,Email}`), `Cc` (same), `Bcc` (flat list of email strings), `Subject`, `Text`, `HTML`, `Attachments` (list of `{Filename, Content(base64), ContentType?, ContentID?}`), `ReplyTo` (list), `Headers` (the `%Swoosh.Email{}.headers` map embedded as a JSON object — Mailpit then writes them into the generated MIME message; restricted headers like `To/From/Subject/...` are rejected by Mailpit itself), `tags` (from `provider_options[:tags]`).
- **Real bodies:** YES — both `text_body` and `html_body` are forwarded to Mailpit's `Text` and `HTML` JSON keys, which Mailpit then renders into the real stored MIME message. Attachments are base64-encoded.
- **Response mapping:** `200..399` → `{:ok, %{id: decoded["ID"]}}`; `>=400` → `{:error, {code, decoded_or_raw_body}}`; network → `{:error, reason}`.
- **Requires an API client** (Finch/Hackney/Req) — see M "Installation".
- Source: `lib/swoosh/adapters/mailpit.ex` on `main`.

---

## 3. Swoosh.ApiClient.Finch

- **Config lines (required):**

```elixir
config :swoosh, :api_client, Swoosh.ApiClient.Finch
```

- **Default Finch instance name is exactly `Swoosh.Finch`** — confirmed by `lib/swoosh/api_client/finch.ex`:

```elixir
defp finch_name do
  Application.get_env(:swoosh, :finch_name, Swoosh.Finch)
end
```

- **Supervision requirement** — you must start a Finch instance. The standard child spec is:

```elixir
children = [
  {Finch, name: Swoosh.Finch}
]
```

If you already have a Finch with a different name (e.g. your app-wide `MyApp.Finch`), point Swoosh at it via the `:finch_name` config key:

```elixir
config :swoosh,
  api_client: Swoosh.ApiClient.Finch,
  finch_name: MyApp.Finch
```

Dynamic start (rare): `Finch.start_link(name: Swoosh.Finch)`.

- **`Swoosh.ApiClient.Finch.init/0` will `Application.ensure_all_started(:finch)` and raise `"missing finch dependency"`** if `:finch` isn't loaded — so you need `{:finch, "~> 0.6", optional: true}` (or whatever current) in `mix.exs`.
- **Client options pass-through:** `email.private[:client_options]` is forwarded as the third arg to `Finch.request/3` — useful for `:receive_timeout`, `:pool_timeout`, etc.
- **User-Agent** is auto-set: `{"User-Agent", "swoosh/<ver>"}`, prepended to the adapter's own headers.
- **Default api_client (fallback):** `Swoosh.ApiClient.Hackney`. This is hard-coded in `mix.exs` under `application`:

```elixir
env: [json_library: Jason, api_client: Swoosh.ApiClient.Hackney]
```

So **if you don't set `config :swoosh, :api_client, ...`, you fall back to `Swoosh.ApiClient.Hackney`** — which will fail to start if `:hackney` isn't in your `mix.exs`. To opt out completely (e.g. for non-HTTP adapters) set `config :swoosh, :api_client, false`.
- **First release of Swoosh.ApiClient.Finch:** **1.4.0** (per changelog). The README still says "defaults to hackney" — Finch has never been auto-defaulted. No version has changed that.
- Source: `lib/swoosh/api_client/finch.ex`, `lib/swoosh/api_client.ex`, `mix.exs` (all on `main`).

---

## 4. Swoosh.Mailer

- **Definition:**

```elixir
defmodule MyApp.Mailer do
  use Swoosh.Mailer, otp_app: :my_app
end
```

The `__using__` macro reads `Application.get_env(otp_app, MyApp.Mailer)` (via `parse_config/4`) at **runtime**, every time `deliver/2` is called. Specifically (from `lib/swoosh/mailer.ex`):

```elixir
defp parse_config(config) do
  Mailer.parse_config(@otp_app, __MODULE__, @mailer_config, config)
end

def parse_config(otp_app, mailer, mailer_config, dynamic_config) do
  Application.get_env(otp_app, mailer, [])
  |> Keyword.merge(mailer_config)            # per-module attrs from `use Swoosh.Mailer, otp_app: :x, adapter: ...`
  |> Keyword.merge(dynamic_config)          # per-call overrides from `deliver(email, adapter: ...)`
  |> interpolate_env_vars()                 # supports {:system, "ENV_VAR"} values, deprecated
end
```

- **Config schema under `config :my_app, MyApp.Mailer`:** the *only* universal key is `:adapter` (read by `Keyword.fetch!(config, :adapter)` in `Swoosh.Mailer.deliver/2`). All other keys are adapter-specific — common ones:
  - `Swoosh.Adapters.Loops` → `:api_key`, optional `:base_url`
  - `Swoosh.Adapters.Mailpit` → `:base_url`, optional `:api_key`
  - `Swoosh.Adapters.SMTP` → `:relay`, `:username`, `:password`, `:tls`, etc.
  - `Swoosh.Adapters.Sendgrid` → `:api_key`
  - `Swoosh.Adapters.Postmark` → `:api_key`
- **Compile-time vs runtime:** adapter/keys are read **at runtime per call** (per the macro above). However, the `validate_dependency/0` callback runs once at module load (`@on_load :validate_dependency`) and will abort compilation/startup if the adapter module isn't loadable or its deps are missing. Once past that, swapping `config :my_app, MyApp.Mailer, adapter: ...` per environment works.
- **Per-environment override:** yes, just put different `config :my_app, MyApp.Mailer, adapter: ...` lines in `config/dev.exs` / `config/test.exs` / `config/prod.exs`.
- **Per-test runtime override:** yes, two clean ways:
  1. `Application.put_env(:my_app, MyApp.Mailer, adapter: Swoosh.Adapters.Test, ...)` in `setup` / `test setup` (it's `Application.get_env`, not compile-time).
  2. Per-call dynamic: `MyApp.Mailer.deliver(email, adapter: Swoosh.Adapters.Test, api_key: "x")` — last-merge-wins via `Keyword.merge(dynamic_config)` in `parse_config/4`. See `Mailer.deliver/2` signature in the `__using__` macro:

```elixir
@spec deliver(Swoosh.Email.t(), Keyword.t()) :: {:ok, term} | {:error, term}
def deliver(email, config \\ [])
```

- **Per-module compile-time override** (highest priority over app config but still merged at runtime):

```elixir
defmodule MyApp.Mailer do
  use Swoosh.Mailer, otp_app: :my_app,
    adapter: Swoosh.Adapters.Loops,
    api_key: "..."
end
```

- **Telemetry:** every call emits `[:swoosh, :deliver, :start|:stop|:exception]` with `metadata = %{mailer: __MODULE__, email: ..., config: ..., result: ..., error: ...}` (set inside the `instrument/3` helper). See Mailer docs "Telemetry" section.
- **`deliver!/2` raises `Swoosh.DeliveryError`** on `{:error, reason}`; otherwise returns the `{:ok, value}` value's right side.
- Source: `lib/swoosh/mailer.ex` on `main`.

---

## 5. Swoosh.TestAssertions + Swoosh.Adapters.Test

- **Wire `Swoosh.Adapters.Test` for tests** (config-based):

```elixir
# config/test.exs
config :my_app, MyApp.Mailer, adapter: Swoosh.Adapters.Test
```

Or per-test:

```elixir
Application.put_env(:my_app, MyApp.Mailer, adapter: Swoosh.Adapters.Test)
# or
MyApp.Mailer.deliver(email, adapter: Swoosh.Adapters.Test)
```

- **Adapter behavior** (`lib/swoosh/adapters/test.ex`): `send(pid, {:email, email})` to the test process **and** every process in `Process.get(:"$callers")`. So if a Phoenix LiveView or Task delivers, you must either be in `$callers` or set `Application.put_env(:swoosh, :shared_test_process, self())` via the helper. There is no global mailbox, no ETS, no process registry.
- **Assertions API** (importable as `import Swoosh.TestAssertions`):

| Function | Form |
|---|---|
| `assert_email_sent()` | asserts any `{:email, _}` was received |
| `assert_email_sent(%Swoosh.Email{})` | exact-struct match (`assert_received {:email, ^email}`) |
| `assert_email_sent([subject: "...", to: "..."])` | keyword map of fields to match |
| `assert_email_sent(fn email -> ... end)` | boolean predicate |
| `assert_email_not_sent(%Swoosh.Email{})` | exact-struct NOT sent |
| `refute_email_sent()` (macro) | no `{:email, _}` received |
| `refute_email_sent(attrs)` (macro) | pattern-match (single value, list-coerced for `to/cc/bcc`) NOT received |
| `assert_emails_sent()` / `assert_emails_sent(emails_or_attrs)` | matches `{:emails, [...]}` from `deliver_many/2` |
| `refute_emails_sent()` (macro) | no `{:emails, _}` received |
| `assert_no_email_sent()` | both `refute_email_sent` and `refute_emails_sent` |
| `set_swoosh_global(context \\ %{})` (test setup callback) | puts `:shared_test_process` to `self()` for the case |

- **Keyword matcher field handling** (in `assert_equal/2`): `subject`, `from`, `reply_to`, `text_body`, `html_body`, `headers` do direct `==`; `subject/text_body/html_body` also accept `%Regex{}`; `to/cc/bcc` accept a single string or list and apply `Swoosh.Email.Recipient.format/1` (so you can write `to: "x@y.com"` or `to: [{"Name","x@y.com"}]` interchangeably). For the *positive* `assert_email_sent(keyword)` form, list fields are matched as **membership** of the formatted recipient in the email's list (`Recipient.format(value) in email.to`), not list equality. For `refute_email_sent(keyword)`, list fields are coerced to a single-element list and pattern-matched (`%{to: ["x@y.com"]} = email`).
- **Per-node / per-process / async:** storage is per-process via `Process.get(:"$callers")`. With `async: true` + `setup :set_swoosh_global`, you get an error (`"Swoosh cannot be set to global mode when the ExUnit case is async"`). For async tests, use either (a) call from within the test process tree (no global needed) or (b) `Swoosh.Adapters.Sandbox` (separate, async-safe testing adapter for feature/E2E — different from `Test`).
- **No `clear_emails/0` exists.** The `Test` adapter is a pure message-pass; messages are consumed by the assertions themselves (`assert_received` removes them from the mailbox) or sit there harmlessly until process exit. There is no `Swoosh.TestAssertions.clear_emails/0`. The closest is `set_swoosh_global/1` which only registers a shared pid — it doesn't clear.
- **Important for async:** the adapter walks `Process.get(:"$callers")`. If a test process delivers an email directly, it works without `set_swoosh_global`. If delivery is fired from a child process spawned by your code (e.g. a Task started via `Task.start/1` without using the test process as ancestor), the assertion won't see it.
- Source: `lib/swoosh/adapters/test.ex`, `lib/swoosh/test_assertions.ex` on `main`.

---

## 6. Error shapes from `Swoosh.Mailer.deliver/2` (api_client-based adapters)

All api_client-based adapters follow the same pattern (Loops, Mailpit, Resend, Sendgrid, Mailgun, etc.) — they `case` on the result of `Swoosh.ApiClient.post/4` (Loops/Mailpit shown above):

| Outcome | Returned by adapter | Returned by `Mailer.deliver/2` |
|---|---|---|
| 2xx/3xx | `{:ok, %{id: ...}}` or `{:ok, %{}}` | `{:ok, %{...}}` |
| 4xx/5xx (any) | `{:error, {status, body}}` where `body` is a decoded JSON map if parseable, else the raw response body string | `{:error, {status, decoded_or_raw}}` — status is the integer, body is a `map()` or `binary()` |
| Network / DNS / refused / timeout | `{:error, reason}` where `reason` is the underlying client term | `{:error, reason}` (passed through unchanged) |
| Missing `from` on `%Swoosh.Email{}` | (never reached) | `{:error, :from_not_set}` (raised in `Mailer.deliver/2` head clause) |

Concrete examples (Finch-based):
- `Finch.request/3` on connection refused → `{:error, %Mint.TransportError{reason: :econnrefused}}` → `{:error, %Mint.TransportError{...}}` bubbles up to `Mailer.deliver/2`.
- `Finch.request/3` on DNS failure → `{:error, %Mint.TransportError{reason: :nxdomain}}`.
- 4xx/5xx → `{:ok, %Finch.Response{status: 401, ...}}` → adapter transforms to `{:error, {401, %{...}}}` or `{:error, {401, "<raw>"}}`.
- **There is no `Swoosh.ApiClientError` struct.** Swoosh does not have such a struct; the only exception is `Swoosh.DeliveryError` (just `defexception fields: [:reason, :payload]`, used by `deliver!/2`), and it is **only raised** by `deliver!`, never returned by `deliver/2`.

How to **classify** 4xx vs 429 vs 5xx vs network from a caller:
- `case result do {:ok, _} -> ... ; {:error, :from_not_set} -> ... ; {:error, {%Mint.TransportError{}, _}} -> :network ; {:error, {code, _body}} when is_integer(code) -> classify(code) end`
- i.e. **inspect the error term's shape**:
  - `is_integer(elem(err, 1))` → it's a `{http_or_smtp_code, body}` tuple from the adapter; use the integer.
  - `elem(err, 0) == %SomeStruct{}` (Mint.TransportError, Req.TransportError, :hackney_connect_timeout, etc.) → network.
  - `:from_not_set` atom → programmer error.

The 429 case is *not* specially treated — it's just another 4xx. If you need 429-specific retry logic you must match `{:error, {429, _}}` yourself.

`Swoosh.DeliveryError` (raised by `deliver!`) formats `:api_error {code, body}` as `"api error - response code: #{code}. body: #{body}"` and `:from_not_set` as `"expected \"from\" to be set"`.

Source: `lib/swoosh/delivery_error.ex`, `lib/swoosh/mailer.ex`, `lib/swoosh/adapters/loops.ex`, `lib/swoosh/adapters/mailpit.ex` on `main`.

---

## 7. Custom headers on `%Swoosh.Email{}`

`Swoosh.Email.header/3` is supported on the struct (see `Swoosh.Email` docs — "headers — a map of headers that should be included in the email"). But how they get onto the wire depends on the **adapter**, not on Swoosh generally:

- **Mailpit (`lib/swoosh/adapters/mailpit.ex`):** the adapter reads `email.headers` and embeds it in the JSON request body under the `"Headers"` key — Mailpit then applies them as **MIME headers on the rendered email**, not as HTTP request headers to Mailpit itself. The HTTP headers to Mailpit are fixed: `Accept`, `Content-Type`, `User-Agent`, optional `Authorization`. Restricted headers (`To/From/Cc/Bcc/Reply-To/Date/Subject/Content-Type/Mime-Version`) are rejected by Mailpit's send handler (per the upstream Mailpit Go code at `server/apiv1/send.go`).
- **Loops (`lib/swoosh/adapters/loops.ex`):** `email.headers` is **completely ignored** by the adapter — the `headers` list sent on the HTTP request is hard-coded to `[Content-Type, User-Agent, Authorization]`. There is no path for `email.header("Idempotency-Key", ...)` to reach the Loops HTTP request — that would require a fork/patch.
- **Other adapters** vary: Resend (added in 1.20.0) maps `email.headers` into a `"headers"` list in the JSON body; Scaleway (1.19.9+) renames them to `"additional_headers"`; Postmark, Sendgrid, Mailgun, etc. all have adapter-specific handling — none of them treat `email.headers` as the HTTP request headers of the call to the provider.

So: `email.header/3` is portable for embedding MIME headers in the *delivered email*, but it is **not** a portable way to set HTTP request headers to the provider. For idempotency, the convention used by some adapters is `put_provider_option(:idempotency_key, ...)` (e.g. Resend, AzureCommunicationServices via `:operation_id`) and a small adapter-side `request_headers/2` to map it to an HTTP header. The Loops adapter currently has no such provider_option.

Source: `lib/swoosh/adapters/*.ex` on `main`; Resend/Scaleway/AzureCommunicationServices headers handling visible in their adapter source.

---

## 8. `gen_smtp` dependency

- **Yes, Swoosh still references `:gen_smtp`, but it is `optional: true`** — from `mix.exs`:

```elixir
{:gen_smtp, "~> 0.13 or ~> 1.0", optional: true},
```

- It's only needed if you use `Swoosh.Adapters.SMTP` (or one of the SMTP-based adapters like `Sendmail`/`AmazonSES` that wraps gen_smtp). The M "Installation" section states this verbatim:

> If you are using `Swoosh.Adapters.SMTP`, `Swoosh.Adapters.Sendmail` or `Swoosh.Adapters.AmazonSES`, you also need to add `gen_smtp` to your dependencies.

- **Mailpit uses the HTTP API** (an API client — Finch/Req/Hackney), not SMTP. So you can drop `gen_smtp` entirely if you only use `Mailpit` + `Loops` + (anything else HTTP-based). Other optional deps you can also drop when you no longer need them: `mail`, `mua`, `cowboy`, `plug`, `plug_cowboy`, `bandit`, `ex_aws`, `hackney` (if you switch to Finch/Req), `multipart` (only required by the Mailgun adapter, per the 1.16.1 changelog).
- **Validate at runtime:** the `validate_dependency/0` callback on each adapter will log an error and abort the VM at startup if the required optional dep isn't loaded. So as long as you don't compile/configure an adapter that needs gen_smtp, removing it is safe.
- Source: `mix.exs`, `lib/swoosh/adapters/smtp.ex` (validate_dependency callback), M "Installation".

---

## 9. Minimum Elixir/OTP

From the top of `lib/swoosh.ex` / `mix.exs` and the M "Requirements":

- **Elixir `~> 1.16`** (mix.exs `elixir: "~> 1.16"`).
- **Erlang/OTP 26+** (M "Requirements" section: "Elixir 1.16+ and Erlang OTP 26+").
- The most recent bump to this floor is visible in changelogs for 1.18.x and was already at 1.16 since 1.17.0. So if `.mise.toml` pins Elixir 1.17 or 1.18, you are comfortably above the floor; the Swoosh `~> 1.26` or `~> 1.27` requirement range you can use is just whatever is in your `mix.exs`.

Practical recommendation for this repo: pin `{:swoosh, "~> 1.26"}` or `~> 1.27` — both work on Elixir 1.17/1.18 with OTP 26+. Anything `~> 1.18` also works but predates `Loops` (1.18.0) and `Mailpit` (1.26.0) — so use 1.26+ to get both.

Source: `mix.exs`, M "Requirements", Swoosh hex.pm page.

---

## Quick decision matrix (relevant to your repo)

| Need | Pin |
|---|---|
| Drop SMTP entirely, run Mailpit over HTTP in dev | `Swoosh.Adapters.Mailpit` + `config :swoosh, :api_client, Swoosh.ApiClient.Finch` + `{Finch, name: Swoosh.Finch}` child; remove `gen_smtp` dep |
| Loops in prod | `Swoosh.Adapters.Loops`; **cannot** set `Idempotency-Key` per request via `email.header/3` (adapter hard-codes its headers); need provider fork or upstream PR if you require per-request idempotency |
| Tests | `config :my_app, MyApp.Mailer, adapter: Swoosh.Adapters.Test` + `import Swoosh.TestAssertions`. For async E2E/LiveView, prefer `Swoosh.Adapters.Sandbox` |
| Error classification in caller | `case Mailer.deliver(email) do {:ok, _} -> ... ; {:error, :from_not_set} -> ... ; {:error, {code, _}} when is_integer(code) -> ... ; {:error, %struct{} = e} -> :network end` — no `Swoosh.ApiClientError` struct exists |
| Finch vs Hackney | Finch is the modern path (1.4.0+), but Hackney is still the explicit `api_client` default in `mix.exs`; **you must opt in with `config :swoosh, :api_client, Swoosh.ApiClient.Finch`** |
| Override adapter per env | `config :my_app, MyApp.Mailer, adapter: ...` per `config/<env>.exs`, OR `MyApp.Mailer.deliver(email, adapter: Swoosh.Adapters.Test)` per call — both supported, config is read at runtime |

defmodule Swoosh.Adapters.Loops do
  @moduledoc ~s"""
  An adapter that sends email using the Loops API.

  For reference: [Loops API docs](https://loops.so/docs/api-reference/send-transactional-email)

  **This adapter requires an API Client.** Swoosh comes with Hackney, Finch and Req out of the box.
  See the [installation section](https://hexdocs.pm/swoosh/Swoosh.html#module-installation)
  for details.

  ## Example

      # config/config.exs
      config :sample, Sample.Mailer,
        adapter: Swoosh.Adapters.Loops,
        api_key: "my-api-key"
      # lib/sample/mailer.ex
      defmodule Sample.Mailer do
        use Swoosh.Mailer, otp_app: :sample
      end

  ## Using with provider options

      import Swoosh.Email

      new()
      |> to("katy@example.com")
      |> from("IGNORED") # see note below
      |> put_provider_option(:data_variables, %{
          "name" => "Chris",
          "passwordResetLink" => "https://example.com/reset-password"
        })
      |> put_provider_option(:transactional_id, "clfq6dinn000yl70fgwwyp82l")

  Note that we need to provide a `from` because it's required by Swoosh. This will
  be ignored though, since Loops API doesn't support setting a sender.

  ## Provider Options

  Supported provider options are the following:

  #### Inserted into request payload

    * `:transactional_id` (string) - The ID of the transactional email to send.

    * `:add_to_audience?` (boolean) - If true, a contact will be created in your audience
      using the email value (if a matching contact doesn’t already exist). Disabled by
      default.

    * `:data_variables` (map) - An object containing data as defined by the data variables
      added to the transactional email template. Values can be of type string or number.
  """

  use Swoosh.Adapter, required_config: [:api_key]

  alias Swoosh.Email

  import Swoosh.Email.Render

  @base_url "https://app.loops.so/api/v1"
  @api_endpoint "/transactional"

  @impl Swoosh.Adapter
  def deliver(%Email{} = email, config \\ []) do
    headers = [
      {"Content-Type", "application/json"},
      {"User-Agent", "swoosh/#{Swoosh.version()}"},
      {"Authorization", "Bearer #{config[:api_key]}"}
    ]

    payload = email |> prepare_payload() |> Swoosh.json_library().encode!
    url = [base_url(config), @api_endpoint]

    case Swoosh.ApiClient.post(url, headers, payload, email) do
      {:ok, code, _headers, _body} when code >= 200 and code <= 399 ->
        {:ok, %{}}

      {:ok, code, _headers, body} when code >= 400 ->
        case Swoosh.json_library().decode(body) do
          {:ok, error} -> {:error, {code, error}}
          {:error, _} -> {:error, {code, body}}
        end

      {:error, reason} ->
        {:error, reason}
    end
  end

  defp base_url(config), do: config[:base_url] || @base_url

  defp prepare_payload(email) do
    %{}
    |> prepare_to(email)
    |> prepare_provider_options_payload_fields(email)
    |> prepare_attachments(email)
  end

  defp prepare_to(payload, %Email{to: to}),
    do: Map.put(payload, "email", render_recipient(to))

  defp prepare_provider_options_payload_fields(payload, %Email{provider_options: provider_options}) do
    Map.merge(payload, %{
      "transactionalId" => provider_options.transactional_id,
      "addToAudience" => provider_options[:add_to_audience?] || false,
      "dataVariables" => provider_options[:data_variables] || %{}
    })
  end

  defp prepare_attachments(payload, %{attachments: []}), do: payload

  defp prepare_attachments(payload, %{attachments: attachments}) do
    Map.put(
      payload,
      "attachments",
      Enum.map(
        attachments,
        &%{
          "filename" => &1.filename,
          "contentType" => &1.content_type,
          "data" => Swoosh.Attachment.get_content(&1, :base64)
        }
      )
    )
  end
end

```elixir
defmodule Dhc.Email.ApiClient do
```

defmodule Swoosh.Adapters.Test do
  @moduledoc ~S"""
  An adapter that sends emails as messages to the current process.

  This is meant to be used during tests and works with the assertions found in
  the [Swoosh.TestAssertions](Swoosh.TestAssertions.html) module.

  For feature, browser, and E2E tests where the email is delivered from
  request-handling or LiveView processes, use the
  [Swoosh.Adapters.Sandbox](Swoosh.Adapters.Sandbox.html) adapter instead.

  ## Example

      # config/test.exs
      config :sample, Sample.Mailer,
        adapter: Swoosh.Adapters.Test

      # lib/sample/mailer.ex
      defmodule Sample.Mailer do
        use Swoosh.Mailer, otp_app: :sample
      end
  """

  use Swoosh.Adapter

  def deliver(email, _config) do
    for pid <- pids() do
      send(pid, {:email, email})
    end

    {:ok, %{}}
  end

  def deliver_many(emails, _config) do
    for pid <- pids() do
      send(pid, {:emails, emails})
    end

    responses = for _email <- emails, do: %{}

    {:ok, responses}
  end

  # Essentially finds all of the processes that tried to send an email (in the test)
  # and sends an email to that process.
  defp pids do
    if pid = Application.get_env(:swoosh, :shared_test_process) do
      [pid]
    else
      Enum.uniq([self() | List.wrap(Process.get(:"$callers"))])
    end
  end
end

defmodule Dhc.Email.WorkerTest do
  # async: false — swaps :environment and the Dhc.Email.Mailer adapter via
  # application env (house seam pattern), which cannot race across tests.
  use ExUnit.Case, async: false

  import Swoosh.TestAssertions

  alias Dhc.Email.Worker

  @job_id 42

  @valid_args %{
    "email" => "user@example.com",
    "transactional_id" => "inviteMember",
    "data_variables" => %{"name" => "Alice", "inviteLink" => "https://example.com/invite"}
  }

  defp job(args, id \\ @job_id), do: %Oban.Job{id: id, args: args}

  setup do
    original_mailer = Application.get_env(:dhc, Dhc.Email.Mailer)
    original_env = Application.get_env(:dhc, :environment)

    on_exit(fn ->
      if original_mailer do
        Application.put_env(:dhc, Dhc.Email.Mailer, original_mailer)
      else
        Application.delete_env(:dhc, Dhc.Email.Mailer)
      end

      Application.put_env(:dhc, :environment, original_env)
    end)

    :ok
  end

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Seam 1: the public worker contract, observed through Swoosh.TestAssertions
  # (test.exs wires Dhc.Email.Mailer to Swoosh.Adapters.Test).
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  describe "perform/1 delivers through the configured mailer" do
    test "sends the email kind and data variables to the recipient" do
      assert Worker.perform(job(@valid_args)) == :ok

      assert_email_sent(fn email ->
        # The friendly name is translated through :loops_transactional_ids
        # (configured in test.exs) before it reaches the provider options.
        assert email.provider_options.transactional_id == "test-loops-id-inviteMember"

        assert email.provider_options.data_variables == %{
                 "name" => "Alice",
                 "inviteLink" => "https://example.com/invite"
               }
      end)

      assert_email_sent(to: "user@example.com")
    end

    test "carries an Idempotency-Key derived from the Oban job id" do
      assert Worker.perform(job(@valid_args)) == :ok

      assert_email_sent(
        to: "user@example.com",
        headers: %{"Idempotency-Key" => "oban-#{@job_id}"}
      )
    end

    test "decorates the message with a JSON summary for the dev inbox" do
      assert Worker.perform(job(@valid_args)) == :ok

      assert_email_sent(fn email ->
        assert email.subject == "[dev] Email: inviteMember"

        payload =
          email.text_body && Jason.decode!(email.text_body)

        assert payload["transactional_id"] == "inviteMember"
        assert payload["data_variables"]["name"] == "Alice"
        assert payload["data_variables"]["inviteLink"] == "https://example.com/invite"
      end)
    end

    test "defaults data_variables to an empty map" do
      args = Map.delete(@valid_args, "data_variables")

      assert Worker.perform(job(args)) == :ok

      assert_email_sent(fn email ->
        assert email.provider_options.data_variables == %{}
      end)
    end

    test "accepts numeric data variable values" do
      args = %{
        "email" => "user@example.com",
        "transactional_id" => "workshopAnnouncement",
        "data_variables" => %{"count" => 5, "name" => "Bob"}
      }

      assert Worker.perform(job(args)) == :ok

      assert_email_sent(fn email ->
        assert email.provider_options.data_variables == %{"count" => 5, "name" => "Bob"}
        assert email.provider_options.transactional_id == "test-loops-id-workshopAnnouncement"
      end)
    end

    test "translates every known friendly name to its mapped template id" do
      mappings = %{
        "inviteMember" => "test-loops-id-inviteMember",
        "workshopAnnouncement" => "test-loops-id-workshopAnnouncement",
        "workshopRegistration" => "test-loops-id-workshopRegistration",
        "workshopRegistrationError" => "test-loops-id-workshopRegistrationError",
        "magicLink" => "test-loops-id-magicLink"
      }

      for {friendly_name, mapped_id} <- mappings do
        args = %{"email" => "user@example.com", "transactional_id" => friendly_name}

        assert Worker.perform(job(args)) == :ok

        assert_email_sent(fn email ->
          assert email.provider_options.transactional_id == mapped_id
        end)
      end
    end
  end

  describe "perform/1 with invalid args" do
    test "returns {:cancel, ...} when email is missing" do
      args = Map.delete(@valid_args, "email")

      assert {:cancel, {:validation, errors}} = Worker.perform(job(args))
      assert "missing email" in errors
    end

    test "returns {:cancel, ...} when email is empty string" do
      args = Map.put(@valid_args, "email", "")

      assert {:cancel, {:validation, errors}} = Worker.perform(job(args))
      assert "missing email" in errors
    end

    test "returns {:cancel, ...} when email has invalid format" do
      args = Map.put(@valid_args, "email", "not-an-email")

      assert {:cancel, {:validation, errors}} = Worker.perform(job(args))
      assert "invalid email format" in errors
    end

    test "returns {:cancel, ...} when transactional_id is missing" do
      args = Map.delete(@valid_args, "transactional_id")

      assert {:cancel, {:validation, errors}} = Worker.perform(job(args))
      assert "missing transactional_id" in errors
    end

    test "returns {:cancel, ...} when transactional_id is unknown" do
      args = Map.put(@valid_args, "transactional_id", "unknownTemplate")

      assert {:cancel, {:validation, errors}} = Worker.perform(job(args))
      assert "invalid transactional_id" in errors
    end

    test "returns {:cancel, ...} when data_variables has non-string/number values" do
      args = put_in(@valid_args, ["data_variables", "link"], %{"nested" => "object"})

      assert {:cancel, {:validation, errors}} = Worker.perform(job(args))
      assert "data_variables values must be strings or numbers" in errors
    end

    test "accumulates multiple validation errors" do
      assert {:cancel, {:validation, errors}} = Worker.perform(job(%{}))
      assert "missing email" in errors
      assert "missing transactional_id" in errors
      assert "invalid transactional_id" in errors
    end

    test "never delivers when args are invalid" do
      refute_email_sent()
      Worker.perform(job(%{}))
      refute_email_sent()
    end
  end

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Seam 2: delivery-failure semantics. The mailer adapter is swapped for a
  # configurable stub (mirroring the :discord_adapter / :onboarding_stripe_adapter
  # seams) so classification can be exercised without real HTTP.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  describe "perform/1 failure semantics in prod" do
    import ExUnit.CaptureLog

    setup do
      Application.put_env(:dhc, :environment, :prod)
      :ok
    end

    test "cancels deterministically when the provider rejects a 4xx validation family response" do
      stub_delivery({:error, {400, %{"message" => "Missing required data variable"}}})

      assert {:cancel, {:provider_rejected, 400}} = Worker.perform(job(@valid_args))
    end

    test "cancels on 422-style unprocessable content" do
      stub_delivery({:error, {422, %{"message" => "unprocessable"}}})

      assert {:cancel, {:provider_rejected, 422}} = Worker.perform(job(@valid_args))
    end

    test "retries on rate limiting (429)" do
      stub_delivery({:error, {429, %{"message" => "rate limited"}}})

      assert {:error, {429, %{"message" => "rate limited"}}} = Worker.perform(job(@valid_args))
    end

    test "retries on provider 5xx" do
      stub_delivery({:error, {503, "upstream unavailable"}})

      assert {:error, {503, "upstream unavailable"}} = Worker.perform(job(@valid_args))
    end

    test "retries on network errors" do
      stub_delivery({:error, %Mint.TransportError{reason: :econnrefused}})

      assert {:error, %Mint.TransportError{reason: :econnrefused}} =
               Worker.perform(job(@valid_args))
    end

    test "logs the failure before returning" do
      stub_delivery({:error, {503, "upstream unavailable"}})

      assert capture_log(fn -> Worker.perform(job(@valid_args)) end) =~ "503"
    end

    test "cancels instead of sending when the template id mapping is absent" do
      original_map = Application.get_env(:dhc, :loops_transactional_ids)
      Application.put_env(:dhc, :loops_transactional_ids, %{})
      stub_delivery({:ok, %{}})

      assert {:cancel, {:transactional_id_not_configured, "inviteMember"}} =
               Worker.perform(job(@valid_args))

      refute_email_sent()
    after
      if original_map,
        do: Application.put_env(:dhc, :loops_transactional_ids, original_map),
        else: Application.delete_env(:dhc, :loops_transactional_ids)
    end

    test "cancels instead of sending when the template id mapping is empty" do
      original_map = Application.get_env(:dhc, :loops_transactional_ids)
      Application.put_env(:dhc, :loops_transactional_ids, %{"inviteMember" => ""})
      stub_delivery({:ok, %{}})

      assert {:cancel, {:transactional_id_not_configured, "inviteMember"}} =
               Worker.perform(job(@valid_args))

      refute_email_sent()
    after
      if original_map,
        do: Application.put_env(:dhc, :loops_transactional_ids, original_map),
        else: Application.delete_env(:dhc, :loops_transactional_ids)
    end
  end

  describe "perform/1 failure semantics outside prod" do
    import ExUnit.CaptureLog

    # environment stays :test (set by config/test.exs); the mailer adapter
    # stands in for a stopped local Mailpit relay.
    test "swallows delivery failures so the dev queue never wedges" do
      stub_delivery({:error, %Mint.TransportError{reason: :econnrefused}})

      logs =
        capture_log(fn ->
          assert Worker.perform(job(@valid_args)) == :ok
        end)

      assert logs =~ "will not retry"
    end

    test "still swallows provider-side rejections outside prod" do
      stub_delivery({:error, {400, %{"message" => "nope"}}})

      assert Worker.perform(job(@valid_args)) == :ok
    end
  end

  defp stub_delivery(result) do
    Application.put_env(:dhc, Dhc.Email.Mailer,
      adapter: Dhc.Email.AdapterStub,
      stub_result: result
    )
  end
end

defmodule Dhc.Email.ApiClientTest do
  use ExUnit.Case, async: true

  alias Dhc.Email.ApiClient
  alias Swoosh.Email

  # Swoosh's first-party adapters hard-code their HTTP request headers, so the
  # repo ships a tiny api_client wrapper that lifts the :idempotency_key
  # provider option onto every provider call as an Idempotency-Key HTTP header
  # (ADR 0021). These tests pin that contract.

  defp email_with(opts) do
    email = %Email{} |> Email.to("user@example.com") |> Email.from("dev@dhc.local")

    Enum.reduce(opts, email, fn {key, value}, acc ->
      Email.put_provider_option(acc, key, value)
    end)
  end

  describe "idempotency_header/2" do
    test "lifts the :idempotency_key provider option into an HTTP header" do
      headers =
        ApiClient.idempotency_header([], email_with(idempotency_key: "oban-#{@job_id()}"))

      assert {"Idempotency-Key", "oban-#{@job_id()}"} in headers
    end

    test "prepends the header without disturbing adapter-supplied headers" do
      base_headers = [{"Content-Type", "application/json"}, {"Authorization", "Bearer sk"}]

      headers =
        ApiClient.idempotency_header(base_headers, email_with(idempotency_key: "oban-7"))

      assert headers == [
               {"Idempotency-Key", "oban-7"},
               {"Content-Type", "application/json"},
               {"Authorization", "Bearer sk"}
             ]
    end

    test "returns the original headers when no idempotency option is set" do
      base_headers = [{"Content-Type", "application/json"}]

      assert ApiClient.idempotency_header(base_headers, email_with([])) == base_headers
    end
  end

  defp @job_id, do: 42
end

```elixir
defmodule Dhc.Email.Worker do
  use Oban.Worker, queue: :emails, max_attempts: 5

  require Logger

  alias Dhc.Email.Mailer

  @transactional_ids ~w(inviteMember workshopAnnouncement workshopRegistration workshopRegistrationError magicLink)

  @impl Worker
  def perform(%Oban.Job{args: args} = job) do
    ctx = job_log_context(job)

    with :ok <- validate_args(args, ctx),
         :ok <- deliver(args, job, ctx) do
      :ok
    else
      {:cancel, _reason} = cancelled -> cancelled
      {:error, reason} = error ->
        Logger.error(... email/transactional metadata ...)
        error
    end
  end
```

Hmm wait — logging placement. validate_args logs+Sentry internally on failure and returns {:cancel,...}. resolve_id logs internally too. Delivery errors: classify() handles logging per branch. So perform's else just passes through without double-logging. Simplify: each stage returns fully-handled results.

```elixir
defp deliver(%{"email" => to, "transactional_id" => kind} = args, %Oban.Job{id: id} = job, ctx) do
  with {:ok, template_id} <- resolve_template_id(kind, ctx),
       email = build_email(to, kind, template_id, Map.get(args, "data_variables", %{}), id),
       :ok <- send_email(email, kind, ctx) do
    :ok
  else
    {:cancel, _} = cancel -> cancel
    {:error, reason} = retry ->
      # already logged in classify
      retry
  end
end

defp build_email(to, kind, template_id, data_variables, oban_job_id) do
  %Swoosh.Email{}
  |> from(email_from())
  |> to(to)
  |> put_provider_option(:transactional_id, template_id)
  |> put_provider_option(:data_variables, data_variables)
  |> maybe_put_idempotency(oban_job_id)
```

Hmm decorate_for_dev needs environment check — pure-ish but reads app env. Fine.

maybe_put_idempotency: if oban_job_id → provider option :idempotency_key "oban-#{id}" AND header("Idempotency-Key", same). 

decorate_for_dev(email, kind, data_vars): unless prod: subject "[dev] Email: #{kind}", text_body pretty JSON %{email:, transactional_id:, data_variables:}. Needs recipient email string → pass to. 

send_email:
```elixir
defp send_email(email, kind, ctx) do
  case Mailer.deliver(email) do
    {:ok, receipt} ->
      Logger.info("[email-worker] Email sent successfully", Keyword.merge(ctx, email: ..., transactional_id: kind))
      :ok
    {:error, reason} -> handle_delivery_error(reason, kind, ctx)
  end
end

defp handle_delivery_error(reason, kind, ctx) do
  if env() == :prod do
    classify(reason, kind, ctx)
  else
    Logger.warning("[email-worker] Dev delivery failed (is Mailpit up?), job will not retry", ...)
    :ok
  end
end

# Deterministic provider rejections: 4xx except rate limiting. Retrying can't
# fix a bad payload/template mapping; discard immediately after capturing.
defp classify({status, _body} = reason, kind, ctx) when is_integer(status) and status >= 400 and status < 500 and status != 429 do
  message = "[email-worker] Provider rejected #{kind} (#{status}); discarding job"
  Logger.error(message, ...)
  Sentry.capture_message(...)
  {:cancel, {:provider_rejected, status}}
end

defp classify(reason, kind, ctx) do
  Logger.error("[email-worker] Transient delivery failure; Oban will retry", ...)
  {:error, reason}
end
```

defmodule Swoosh.ApiClient.Finch do
  @moduledoc """
  Finch-based ApiClient for Swoosh.

      config :swoosh, :api_client, Swoosh.ApiClient.Finch

  In order to use `Finch` API client, you must start `Finch` and provide a :name.
  Often in your supervision tree:

      children = [
        {Finch, name: Swoosh.Finch}
      ]

  Or, in rare cases, dynamically:

      Finch.start_link(name: Swoosh.Finch)

  If a name different from `Swoosh.Finch` is used, or you want to use an existing Finch instance,
  you can provide the name via the config.

      config :swoosh,
        api_client: Swoosh.ApiClient.Finch,
        finch_name: My.Custom.Name
  """

  require Logger

  @behaviour Swoosh.ApiClient
  @user_agent {"User-Agent", "swoosh/#{Swoosh.version()}"}

  @impl true
  def init do
    unless Code.ensure_loaded?(Finch) do
      Logger.error("""
      Could not find finch dependency.

      Please add :finch to your dependencies:

          {:finch, "~> 0.8"}

      Or set your own Swoosh.ApiClient:

          config :swoosh, :api_client, MyAPIClient
      """)

      raise "missing finch dependency"
    end

    _ = Application.ensure_all_started(:finch)
    :ok
  end

  @impl true
  def post(url, headers, body, %Swoosh.Email{} = email) do
    url = IO.iodata_to_binary(url)
    request = Finch.build(:post, url, [@user_agent | headers], body)
    options = email.private[:client_options] || []

    case Finch.request(request, finch_name(), options) do
      {:ok, response} ->
        {:ok, response.status, response.headers, response.body}

      {:error, reason} ->
        {:error, reason}
    end
  end

  defp finch_name do
    Application.get_env(:swoosh, :finch_name, Swoosh.Finch)
  end
end

defmodule Dhc.Email.ApiClient do
  @moduledoc """
  Swoosh api_client that adds an Idempotency-Key HTTP header to every
  outgoing provider request (ADR 0021).

  Swoosh's first-party adapters hard-code their HTTP request headers, so an
  `Idempotency-Key` set via `Swoosh.Email.header/3` never reaches the wire.
  This client wraps `Swoosh.ApiClient.Finch` and lifts the
  `:idempotency_key` provider option onto the request instead:

      email
      |> put_provider_option(:idempotency_key, "oban-1234")
      |> Dhc.Email.Mailer.deliver()
      # => POST with header {"Idempotency-Key", "oban-1234"}

  Because it sits below the adapter layer, the header survives the Loops →
  Resend cutover unchanged. Remove this wrapper if upstream Swoosh ever grows
  first-party idempotency support.

  Wired globally via `config :swoosh, api_client: Dhc.Email.ApiClient`; the
  Finch instance is named by `config :swoosh, :finch_name` (default
  `Swoosh.Finch`, supervised in `Dhc.Application`).
  """

  @behaviour Swoosh.ApiClient

  @header_name "Idempotency-Key"

  @impl true
  def init, do: Swoosh.ApiClient.Finch.init()

  @impl true
  def post(url, headers, body, %Swoosh.Email{} = email) do
    Swoosh.ApiClient.Finch.post(url, idempotency_header(headers, email), body, email)
  end

  @doc """
  Prepends `{"Idempotency-Key", key}` to `headers` when `email` carries the
  `:idempotency_key` provider option; returns `headers` untouched otherwise.
  """
  @spec idempotency_header(Swoosh.ApiClient.headers(), Swoosh.Email.t()) ::
          Swoosh.ApiClient.headers()
  def idempotency_header(headers, %Swoosh.Email{provider_options: provider_options}) do
    case provider_options[:idempotency_key] do
      nil -> headers
      key when is_binary(key) -> [{@header_name, key} | headers]
    end
  end
end

defmodule Dhc.Email.Worker do
  @moduledoc """
  Oban worker that sends transactional emails through the Swoosh transport
  seam (ADR 0021 — Swoosh Is the Email Transport Seam).

  Migrated from the `process-emails` Deno edge function. Each job represents
  a single email (one Oban job per message, replacing the pgmq batch-read
  pattern).

  ## Job args (public contract — unchanged)

    * `email` — the recipient email address
    * `transactional_id` — a friendly template name (`"inviteMember"`,
      `"workshopAnnouncement"`, `"workshopRegistration"`,
      `"workshopRegistrationError"`, `"magicLink"`). The worker translates
      this to the provider's dashboard-generated template ID via the
      `:loops_transactional_ids` app env map.
    * `data_variables` — key-value pairs injected into the email template
      (values must be strings or numbers)

  ## Delivery

  The worker builds one `%Swoosh.Email{}` per job — recipient, sender, and
  provider options (`transactional_id`, `data_variables`) — and hands it to
  `Dhc.Email.Mailer`. Which provider actually delivers is environment config,
  not code: `Swoosh.Adapters.Loops` in prod, `Swoosh.Adapters.Mailpit` over
  HTTP in dev (`http://localhost:8025` web UI), `Swoosh.Adapters.Test` in
  tests.

  Outside prod the message is decorated with a JSON summary body
  (recipient + friendly Kind + data variables) so the dev inbox shows who
  would receive what; providers render real bodies from their templates.

  ## Idempotency

  Every send carries an `Idempotency-Key` derived from the Oban job id
  (`oban-<job.id>`), applied at the HTTP layer by `Dhc.Email.ApiClient`.
  Provider retries therefore cannot double-send a delivered email.

  ## Error classification

    * Invalid job args and unmapped/empty template IDs are deterministic:
      the job is **cancelled immediately** (`{:cancel, _}`) with a Sentry
      capture instead of burning five identical attempts.
    * In prod, provider responses of 4xx (except 429 rate limiting) are
      deterministic rejections too: cancelled with Sentry capture. Rate
      limits, 5xx, and network errors are transient: returned as
      `{:error, reason}` for Oban's exponential-backoff retries
      (`max_attempts: 5`).
    * Outside prod, delivery failures are logged and swallowed (`:ok`) —
      a stopped Mailpit container must never fail or retry dev jobs.

  ## Logging

  Every log line carries the Oban job context (`oban_job_id`, `oban_attempt`,
  `oban_queue`, `oban_worker`) plus `email` and `transactional_id`, so
  failures can be correlated to a specific job.
  """

  use Oban.Worker, queue: :emails, max_attempts: 5

  require Logger

  alias Dhc.Email.Mailer
  alias Swoosh.Email

  @transactional_ids ~w(inviteMember workshopAnnouncement workshopRegistration workshopRegistrationError magicLink)
  @idempotency_header "Idempotency-Key"

  @impl Worker
  def perform(%Oban.Job{args: args} = job) do
    ctx = job_log_context(job)

    with :ok <- validate_args(args, ctx),
         :ok <- deliver(args, job, ctx) do
      :ok
    else
      {:cancel, _reason} = cancelled -> cancelled
      {:error, _reason} = retryable -> retryable
    end
  end

  # -- Argument validation ----------------------------------------------------

  defp validate_args(args, ctx) do
    errors =
      []
      |> validate_required(args, "email")
      |> validate_email_format(args)
      |> validate_required(args, "transactional_id")
      |> validate_transactional_id(args)
      |> validate_data_variables(args)

    case errors do
      [] ->
        :ok

      errors ->
        message = "Invalid email job args: #{Enum.join(errors, ", ")}"

        Logger.error(
          "[email-worker] #{message}",
          Keyword.merge(ctx,
            email: args["email"],
            transactional_id: args["transactional_id"],
            validation_errors: Enum.join(errors, ", ")
          )
        )

        Sentry.capture_message(message,
          level: :error,
          extra: %{
            args: args,
            validation_errors: errors,
            oban_job_id: ctx[:oban_job_id],
            oban_attempt: ctx[:oban_attempt],
            oban_queue: ctx[:oban_queue],
            oban_worker: ctx[:oban_worker]
          }
        )

        {:cancel, {:validation, errors}}
    end
  end

  defp validate_required(errors, args, field) do
    if is_nil(args[field]) or args[field] == "" do
      ["missing #{field}" | errors]
    else
      errors
    end
  end

  defp validate_email_format(errors, %{"email" => email}) when is_binary(email) do
    if email =~ ~r/^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/ do
      errors
    else
      ["invalid email format" | errors]
    end
  end

  defp validate_email_format(errors, _args), do: errors

  defp validate_transactional_id(errors, %{"transactional_id" => id})
       when id in @transactional_ids,
       do: errors

  defp validate_transactional_id(errors, _args),
    do: ["invalid transactional_id" | errors]

  defp validate_data_variables(errors, %{"data_variables" => vars}) when is_map(vars) do
    invalid_values =
      Enum.any?(vars, fn
        {_k, v} when is_binary(v) -> false
        {_k, v} when is_number(v) -> false
        _ -> true
      end)

    if invalid_values do
      ["data_variables values must be strings or numbers" | errors]
    else
      errors
    end
  end

  defp validate_data_variables(errors, _args), do: errors

  # -- Delivery ----------------------------------------------------------------

  defp deliver(
         %{"email" => recipient, "transactional_id" => kind} = args,
         %Oban.Job{} = job,
         ctx
       ) do
    with {:ok, template_id} <- resolve_template_id(kind, ctx) do
      data_variables = Map.get(args, "data_variables", %{})

      recipient
      |> build_email(kind, template_id, data_variables, job.id)
      |> deliver_email(kind, ctx)
    end
  end

  defp resolve_template_id(friendly_name, ctx) do
    # Translation mirrors the edge function's env-var lookup. The map is built
    # in config/runtime.exs / config/dev.exs from *_TRANSACTIONAL_ID env vars.
    # We never send the friendly name to the provider (it 404s there); an
    # unmapped or empty mapping is a deterministic configuration failure.
    map = Application.get_env(:dhc, :loops_transactional_ids, %{})

    case Map.get(map, friendly_name) do
      template_id when is_binary(template_id) and template_id != "" ->
        {:ok, template_id}

      _ ->
        message = "No template ID mapped for transactional_id"

        Logger.error(
          "[email-worker] #{message}",
          Keyword.merge(ctx, transactional_id: friendly_name)
        )

        Sentry.capture_message(message,
          level: :error,
          extra: %{
            transactional_id: friendly_name,
            oban_job_id: ctx[:oban_job_id],
            oban_attempt: ctx[:oban_attempt],
            oban_queue: ctx[:oban_queue],
            oban_worker: ctx[:oban_worker]
          }
        )

        {:cancel, {:transactional_id_not_configured, friendly_name}}
    end
  end

  defp build_email(recipient, kind, template_id, data_variables, oban_job_id) do
    email =
      Email.new()
      |> Email.from(email_from())
      |> Email.to(recipient)
      |> Email.put_provider_option(:transactional_id, template_id)
      |> Email.put_provider_option(:data_variables, data_variables)

    if oban_job_id do
      key = "oban-#{oban_job_id}"

      email
      |> Email.put_provider_option(:idempotency_key, key)
      # MIME-level copy for dev-inbox observability; the wire header comes from
      # the provider option via Dhc.Email.ApiClient.
      |> Email.header(@idempotency_header, key)
    else
      email
    end
    |> decorate_for_dev(recipient, kind, data_variables)
  end

  # Non-prod only: providers render real bodies from their templates, so the
  # dev inbox gets a JSON summary (recipient + friendly Kind + variables).
  defp decorate_for_dev(email, recipient, kind, data_variables) do
    if env() == :prod do
      email
    else
      payload = %{
        email: recipient,
        transactional_id: kind,
        data_variables: data_variables
      }

      subject = "[dev] Email: #{kind}"
      body = Jason.encode!(payload, pretty: true)

      email
      |> Email.subject(subject)
      |> Email.text_body(body)
    end
  end

  defp deliver_email(%Email{} = email, kind, ctx) do
    case Mailer.deliver(email) do
      {:ok, receipt} ->
        Logger.info(
          "[email-worker] Email sent successfully",
          Keyword.merge(ctx,
            email: kind_recipient(email),
            transactional_id: kind,
            receipt: inspect(receipt)
          )
        )

        :ok

      {:error, reason} ->
        handle_delivery_error(reason, kind, ctx)
    end
  end

  defp handle_delivery_error(reason, kind, ctx) do
    if env() == :prod do
      classify_delivery_error(reason, kind, ctx)
    else
      Logger.warning(
        "[email-worker] Dev relay delivery failed (is `docker compose up -d mailpit` running?), job will not retry",
        Keyword.merge(ctx,
          transactional_id: kind,
          reason: inspect(reason)
        )
      )

      :ok
    end
  end

  # Deterministic rejections (4xx except rate limiting): retrying cannot fix a
  # bad payload or template mapping, so cancel immediately with a Sentry
  # capture rather than burn all attempts.
  defp classify_delivery_error({status, _body}, kind, ctx)
       when is_integer(status) and status >= 400 and status < 500 and status != 429 do
    message = "Provider rejected #{kind}; discarding job"

    Logger.error(
      "[email-worker] #{message}",
      Keyword.merge(ctx,
        transactional_id: kind,
        provider_status: status
      )
    )

    Sentry.capture_message(message,
      level: :error,
      extra: %{
        transactional_id: kind,
        provider_status: status,
        oban_job_id: ctx[:oban_job_id],
        oban_attempt: ctx[:oban_attempt],
        oban_queue: ctx[:oban_queue],
        oban_worker: ctx[:oban_worker]
      }
    )

    {:cancel, {:provider_rejected, status}}
  end

  # Rate limits (429), 5xx, and network errors are transient — let Oban retry
  # with backoff. The Idempotency-Key makes those retries safe against
  # double-sends that were already accepted.
  defp classify_delivery_error(reason, kind, ctx) do
    Logger.error(
      "[email-worker] Transient delivery failure; Oban will retry",
      Keyword.merge(ctx,
        transactional_id: kind,
        reason: inspect(reason)
      )
    )

    {:error, reason}
  end

  # -- Environment & helpers ---------------------------------------------------

  defp env do
    Application.get_env(:dhc, :environment, :development)
  end

  # Swoosh requires a sender on every message. Loops ignores it (templates
  # define the sender); Mailpit shows it in the dev inbox.
  defp email_from do
    Application.get_env(:dhc, :email_from, "dev@dhc.local")
  end

  defp kind_recipient(%Email{to: [{_, recipient}]}) when is_binary(recipient), do: recipient
  defp kind_recipient(%Email{to: to}), do: inspect(to)

  defp job_log_context(%Oban.Job{} = job) do
    [
      oban_job_id: job.id,
      oban_attempt: job.attempt,
      oban_queue: job.queue,
      oban_worker: job.worker
    ]
  end
end

parts.text:
Compile error: `original_map` in the `after` block isn't visible — `after` blocks don't see variables bound inside the implicit try of a test unless bound before... Actually in ExUnit tests, `after` blocks only have access to outer variables? The issue: I assigned original_map INSIDE the test body then used it in after. Elixir's test macro wraps body; `after` should close over... apparently not for variables bound in test body (ExUnit's test macro turns into try/after where after can't reference vars bound in body — right, `after` is a separate block scope).

Fix: move the map save/restore into the describe-level setup or use on_exit with a captured value via anonymous function closure:

```elixir
test "..." do
  original_map = Application.get_env(:dhc, :loops_transactional_ids)
  Application.put_env(:dhc, :loops_transactional_ids, %{})
  stub_delivery({:ok, %{}})

  on_exit(fn ->
    if original_map ... 
```

Wait — does on_exit closure capture work? on_exit receives a fun that captures bindings from the test process at registration time — yes, closures capture by value at definition. That works.

Simpler: use setup-based approach or just restore within the test body itself at the end (but assertion failure would skip restore → leak to other tests). on_exit closure is the clean fix.
The `after` block can't see test-body variables — switching to `on_exit` closures which capture bindings:

parts.text:
Interesting: "The process mailbox is empty" on the FIRST test in the describe — but the worker logged "Email sent successfully"? No wait, look at the failure: test at line 43 "sends the email kind and data variables to the recipient" — assert at line 57 failed with mailbox empty. Hmm, but other delivery tests passed (23/24). Why would THIS one have an empty mailbox?

Ah — I see it. The previous test run order: ExUnit runs tests alphabetically-ish? The failing test is the first test in the file. Prior tests in the same file that ran BEFORE it may have consumed... no, mailbox empty means the email was never sent to this process OR was consumed by an earlier assertion.

Wait — actually, look more carefully. In my first test I call `assert_email_sent(fn ...)` twice (once for provider options predicate, once for `to:`). First assert_email_sent consumes the {:email, _} message via assert_received! Then the second assert_email_sent finds the mailbox empty.

From the TestAssertions source: assert_email_sent(params) → assert_received-based; consuming. So each assertion eats a message. Tests that pass do exactly one assert_email_sent... except "translates every known friendly name" does 5 (one per iteration) — that works since each perform sends one email then one assertion consumes it.

Fix: single predicate assertion per delivery covering all fields:

```elixir
assert_email_sent(fn email ->
  assert email.to == [{nil, "user@example.com"}] or use Recipient
  ...
end)
```

For the to: check within a predicate, what's the stored shape? Swoosh Email.to: list of {name, recipient} tuples where name may be nil. `to("user@example.com")` → parse_recipient → {nil, "user@example.com"}? Let me just pattern match loosely: `assert [{"", "user@example.com"}] = email.to or [{"nil"...` — safer: import Swoosh.Email.Recipient? Simplest: assert Enum.any?(email.to, fn {_name, addr} -> addr == "user@example.com" end).

Also the second assertion in the Idempotency-Key test uses keyword form once only — fine. And JSON-summary test uses single predicate — fine.

Rewrite the failing test to one predicate + keep everything inside it.
Found it — `assert_email_sent` **consumes** messages (`assert_received`), so calling it twice for one delivered email empties the mailbox. Merging into a single predicate:

input.newString:
test "sends the email kind and data variables to the recipient" do
      assert Worker.perform(job(@valid_args)) == :ok

      # One delivered email per job; assert everything on that single message
      # because assertions consume mailbox messages.
      assert_email_sent(fn email ->
        # The friendly name is translated through :loops_transactional_ids
        # (configured in test.exs) before it reaches the provider options.
        assert email.provider_options.transactional_id == "test-loops-id-inviteMember"

        assert email.provider_options.data_variables == %{
                 "name" => "Alice",
                 "inviteLink" => "https://example.com/invite"
               }

        assert Enum.any?(email.to, fn {_name, address} ->
                 address == "user@example.com"
               end)
      end)
    end

## Queues / Oban

- **Queues**: pgmq → Oban. Big-bang per-queue cutover. Discord → Email → Announcements → Stripe → Bulk Invite.
- **Loops transactional email**: `Dhc.Email.Worker` (queue `:emails`, `max_attempts: 5`) sends via the Loops.so REST API (`POST https://app.loops.so/api/v1/transactional`) using a hand-rolled `Req.post/2` adapter — no Swoosh/Bamboo. Job args carry a **friendly name** (`inviteMember`/`workshopAnnouncement`/`workshopRegistration`/`workshopRegistrationError`); the worker translates it to the real Loops dashboard ID via the `:loops_transactional_ids` app-env map (built in `config/runtime.exs` + `config/dev.exs` from the `INVITE_MEMBER_TRANSACTIONAL_ID`/`WORKSHOP_ANNOUNCEMENT_TRANSACTIONAL_ID`/`WORKSHOP_REGISTRATION_TRANSACTIONAL_ID`/`WORKSHOP_REGISTRATION_ERROR_TRANSACTIONAL_ID` env vars, all provisioned in `fnox.toml`). This mirrors the edge function's env-var lookup. Only `workshopRegistration` has a real Loops ID as its fallback default (`cmnok76cq02tq0ix92oeoi1kk`); the other three **must** be set in prod or the worker fails fast with `{:error, {:transactional_id_not_configured, name}}` — it never sends the friendly name to Loops (that produces a 404 after 5 retries, as seen in Sentry DHC-API-16). Producers: `Dhc.WorkshopAnnouncements.Worker` (fans out 1 email job per active member), `Dhc.Invitations.BulkInviteWorker` + `Dhc.Invitations.resend_invitation_emails/1` (enqueue `inviteMember` per invite).
- **Worker logging convention**: Every Oban worker log line carries the job context as keyword metadata (`oban_job_id`, `oban_attempt`, `oban_queue`, `oban_worker`) plus domain-specific keys (`email`, `transactional_id`, `loops_id`, `loops_status`, `workshop_id`, `announcement_type`, `created_by`, `invitation_id`, etc.). These keys are registered in three places that must stay in sync when adding new metadata: (1) `config :logger, :default_formatter, metadata: [...]` in `config/config.exs` (local logs), (2) `config :sentry, logs: [metadata: [...]]` in `config/config.exs` + `config/runtime.exs` (Sentry Logs), (3) `Sentry.LoggerHandler` `metadata: [...]` in `config/runtime.exs` (Sentry error events from Logger). `Sentry.capture_message/2` in this Sentry version (13.1.0) does **not** accept `:contexts` — pass Oban context via `:extra` as a flat map. To avoid Sentry PII redaction (`reason: [Filtered]`) on error tuples that contain emails, pass reasons through a `reason_to_map/1` helper that stringifies keys/values rather than `inspect/1`.

## API design / clients

- **API design**: Spec-first with OpenAPI. Custom Mix task generates Phoenix controller stubs. TypeScript client generated from spec.
- **PostgREST read migration**: Replace SvelteKit `supabase.from(...).select(...)` reads with domain-shaped Phoenix APIs, not table/view proxies. Track remaining call sites in [postgrest-read-migration.md](postgrest-read-migration.md); first slice is Waitlist per ADR 0005.

## Queues / Oban

- **Queues**: pgmq → Oban. Big-bang per-queue cutover. Discord → Email → Announcements → Stripe → Bulk Invite.
- **Loops transactional email**: `Dhc.Email.Worker` (queue `:emails`, `max_attempts: 5`) sends via the Loops.so REST API (`POST https://app.loops.so/api/v1/transactional`) using a hand-rolled `Req.post/2` adapter — no Swoosh/Bamboo. Job args carry a **friendly name** (`inviteMember`/`workshopAnnouncement`/`workshopRegistration`/`workshopRegistrationError`); the worker translates it to the real Loops dashboard ID via the `:loops_transactional_ids` app-env map (built in `config/runtime.exs` + `config/dev.exs` from the `INVITE_MEMBER_TRANSACTIONAL_ID`/`WORKSHOP_ANNOUNCEMENT_TRANSACTIONAL_ID`/`WORKSHOP_REGISTRATION_TRANSACTIONAL_ID`/`WORKSHOP_REGISTRATION_ERROR_TRANSACTIONAL_ID` env vars, all provisioned in `fnox.toml`). This mirrors the edge function's env-var lookup. Only `workshopRegistration` has a real Loops ID as its fallback default (`cmnok76cq02tq0ix92oeoi1kk`); the other three **must** be set in prod or the worker fails fast with `{:error, {:transactional_id_not_configured, name}}` — it never sends the friendly name to Loops (that produces a 404 after 5 retries, as seen in Sentry DHC-API-16). Producers: `Dhc.WorkshopAnnouncements.Worker` (fans out 1 email job per active member), `Dhc.Invitations.BulkInviteWorker` + `Dhc.Invitations.resend_invitation_emails/1` (enqueue `inviteMember` per invite).
- **Worker logging convention**: Every Oban worker log line carries the job context as keyword metadata (`oban_job_id`, `oban_attempt`, `oban_queue`, `oban_worker`) plus domain-specific keys (`email`, `transactional_id`, `loops_id`, `loops_status`, `workshop_id`, `announcement_type`, `created_by`, `invitation_id`, etc.). These keys are registered in three places that must stay in sync when adding new metadata: (1) `config :logger, :default_formatter, metadata: [...]` in `config/config.exs` (local logs), (2) `config :sentry, logs: [metadata: [...]]` in `config/config.exs` + `config/runtime.exs` (Sentry Logs), (3) `Sentry.LoggerHandler` `metadata: [...]` in `config/runtime.exs` (Sentry error events from Logger). `Sentry.capture_message/2` in this Sentry version (13.1.0) does **not** accept `:contexts` — pass Oban context via `:extra` as a flat map. To avoid Sentry PII redaction (`reason: [Filtered]`) on error tuples that contain emails, pass reasons through a `reason_to_map/1` helper that stringifies keys/values rather than `inspect/1`.

## API design / clients

- **API design**: Spec-first with OpenAPI. Custom Mix task generates Phoenix controller stubs. TypeScript client generated from spec.
- **PostgREST read migration**: Replace SvelteKit `supabase.from(...).select(...)` reads with domain-shaped Phoenix APIs, not table/view proxies. Track remaining call sites in [postgrest-read-migration.md](postgrest-read-migration.md); first slice is Waitlist per ADR 0005.
- **`.remote.ts` files**: The swap point. Rewrite from `executeWithRLS()` to `fetch(apiClient)` per domain.

input.newString:
## Dev email catching (Mailpit)

The compose file ships a `mailpit` service (`axllent/mailpit`). In dev, the
email worker (`Dhc.Email.Worker`) delivers through Swoosh's Mailpit **HTTP**
adapter (ADR 0021): each job arrives as a real message whose body is the
pretty-printed JSON summary (recipient, friendly template name, data
variables), since only the provider can render the real templates. Web UI at
`http://localhost:8025` (override with `MAILPIT_HTTP_URL`; the SMTP port 1025
is no longer used). Messages are in-memory and lost on container restart. A
stopped Mailpit container is not an error: delivery failures log a warning and
the job still succeeds.
input.oldString:
## Dev email catching (Mailpit)

The compose file ships a `mailpit` service (`axllent/mailpit`). In dev, the
email worker (`Dhc.Email.Worker`) relays every email job to it over SMTP
instead of calling the Loops API — the raw payload (recipient, template name,
data variables) arrives as pretty-printed JSON, since only Loops can render
the real templates. Web UI at `http://localhost:8025`, SMTP on
`localhost:1025` (override with `MAILPIT_HOST`/`MAILPIT_PORT`). Messages are
in-memory and lost on container restart. A stopped Mailpit container is not an
error: delivery failures log a warning and the job still succeeds.
`Dhc.Email.DevMailer` belongs under `apps/phoenix/dev/` because `gen_smtp` is a
dev-only dependency; placing the adapter under `lib/` breaks test-environment
compilation under `--warnings-as-errors`.

<skill_content name="code-review">
# Skill: code-review

Two-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:

- **Standards** — does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?
- **Spec** — does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?

Both axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.

The issue tracker should have been provided to you — run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` if `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing.

## Process

### 1. Pin the fixed point

Whatever the user said is the fixed point — a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc. If they didn't specify one, ask for it.

Capture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.

Before going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here — not inside two parallel sub-agents.

### 2. Identify the spec source

Look for the originating spec, in this order:

1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.) — fetch via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.
2. A path the user passed as an argument.
3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.
4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report "no spec available".

### 3. Identify the standards sources

Anything in the repo that documents how code should be written, such as `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

On top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below — a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:

- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.
- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic ("possible Feature Envy"), never a hard violation — and, like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.

Each smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:

- **Mysterious Name** — a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.
- **Duplicated Code** — the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.
- **Feature Envy** — a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.
- **Data Clumps** — the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.
- **Primitive Obsession** — a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.
- **Repeated Switches** — the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.
- **Shotgun Surgery** — one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.
- **Divergent Change** — one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.
- **Speculative Generality** — abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.
- **Message Chains** — long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.
- **Middle Man** — a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.
- **Refused Bequest** — a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.

### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel

Send a single message with two `Agent` tool calls. Use the `general-purpose` subagent for both.

**Standards sub-agent prompt** — include:

- The full diff command and commit list.
- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full — the sub-agent has no other access to it.
- The brief: "Report — per file/hunk where relevant — (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls — documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words."

**Spec sub-agent prompt** — include:

- The diff command and commit list.
- The path or fetched contents of the spec.
- The brief: "Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words."

If the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.

### 5. Aggregate

Present the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings — the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).

End with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes — that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.

## Why two axes

A change can pass one axis and fail the other:

- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**
- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**

Reporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.

    email =
      Email.new()
      |> Email.from(email_from())
      |> Email.to(recipient)
      |> Email.put_provider_option(:transactional_id, template_id)
      |> Email.put_provider_option(:data_variables, data_variables)

    if oban_job_id do
      key = "oban-#{oban_job_id}"

      email
      |> Email.put_provider_option(:idempotency_key, key)
      # MIME-level copy for dev-inbox observability; the wire header comes from
      # the provider option via Dhc.Email.ApiClient.
      |> Email.header(@idempotency_header, key)

      email
    end

  end

  # dev inbox gets a JSON summary (recipient + friendly Kind + variables).
  defp decorate_for_dev(email, recipient, kind, data_variables) do
    if env() == :prod do
      email
    else
      payload = %{
        email: recipient,
        transactional_id: kind,
        data_variables: data_variables
      }

      subject = "[dev] Email: #{kind}"

      email
      |> Email.subject(subject)
      |> Email.text_body(body)
    end
  end

display.text:
Logger.error(
      "[email-worker] #{message}",
      Keyword.merge(ctx,
        transactional_id: kind,
        provider_status: status
      )
    )

    Sentry.capture_message(message,
      level: :error,
      extra: %{
        transactional_id: kind,
        provider_status: status,
        oban_job_id: ctx[:oban_job_id],
        oban_attempt: ctx[:oban_attempt],
        oban_queue: ctx[:oban_queue],
        oban_worker: ctx[:oban_worker]
      }
    )

    {:cancel, {:provider_rejected, status}}
  end

  # Rate limits (429), 5xx, and network errors are transient — let Oban retry
  # with backoff. The Idempotency-Key makes those retries safe against
  # double-sends that were already accepted.
  defp classify_delivery_error(reason, kind, ctx) do
    Logger.error(
      "[email-worker] Transient delivery failure; Oban will retry",
      Keyword.merge(ctx,
        transactional_id: kind,
        reason: inspect(reason)
      )
    )

    {:error, reason}
  end

  # -- Environment & helpers ---------------------------------------------------

  defp env do
    Application.get_env(:dhc, :environment, :development)
  end

  # Swoosh requires a sender on every message. Loops ignores it (templates
  # define the sender); Mailpit shows it in the dev inbox.
  defp email_from do
    Application.get_env(:dhc, :email_from, "dev@dhc.local")
  end

  defp kind_recipient(%Email{to: [{_, recipient}]}) when is_binary(recipient), do: recipient
  defp kind_recipient(%Email{to: to}), do: inspect(to)

  defp job_log_context(%Oban.Job{} = job) do
    [
      oban_job_id: job.id,
      oban_attempt: job.attempt,
      oban_queue: job.queue,
      oban_worker: job.worker
    ]
  end
end
